small_guidance:
- The kernel reloads the same input slice for every OC tile; since OC=128 and BLOCK_M=128 covers it in one pass, drop the OC outer loop and merge the bias+scale+min into a single accumulator pass — also try BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=16 (and 32) at num_warps=8, num_stages=2 to maximize spatial reuse of weight tiles.
- Add larger spatial tiles (BLOCK_N=256) and smaller OC tiles (BLOCK_M=64) to the autotune list since OC*OUT_HW is dominated by spatial (64516); ensure SMEM stays under budget, e.g. (128·32 + 32·128)·4·2 ≈ 64KB is safe.
- Switch input to channels-last storage (or load with stride_xc=1) so the K dimension (ic·kh·kw with ic innermost) is contiguous and `tl.dot` loads coalesce; currently stride_xc=H*W makes the K-axis loads strided.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as one program per (N, output-spatial tile) with a persistent OC accumulator: load a BLOCK_N spatial tile of im2col columns once into SMEM, then sweep all OC in registers maintaining a running min, eliminating the redundant x reloads across OC tiles that the current 2-level loop incurs.
- Use channels-last (NHWC) input layout so the GEMM-K reduction (ic·kh·kw with ic innermost) is contiguous; this typically 2-3× the effective HBM bandwidth on conv-as-GEMM kernels and is the dominant bottleneck here at H=W=256.
- Fuse the channel-min reduction directly into the OC loop epilogue (no need to materialize the [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N] tile to SMEM): after each OC-block GEMM, apply bias+scale and reduce to [BLOCK_N] via tl.min then combine with the running min — keeps the working set in registers and lets BLOCK_N grow.
